os.label: macOS
os.hint: Uses Homebrew. Install it first from brew.sh if `brew` is missing.

os.label: Windows
os.hint: Run PowerShell as Administrator. winget ships with Windows 10 (21H2+) and 11.

os.label: Ubuntu / Debian
os.hint: Also works on Linux Mint, Pop!_OS and WSL2 Ubuntu.

os.label: Fedora / RHEL
os.hint: Also works on Rocky, AlmaLinux and CentOS Stream (see the RHEL notes).

os.label: Arch Linux
os.hint: Also works on Manjaro and EndeavourOS.

tools.name: Docker
tools.what: Container runtime. kind runs every Kubernetes node as a Docker container, so Docker must be running before anything else.

mac.note: Wait for the whale icon in the menu bar to stop animating before running docker commands.

windows.title: 2. Install Docker Desktop
windows.note: Start Docker Desktop from the Start menu and keep "Use the WSL 2 based engine" checked in Settings → General.

ubuntu.code:
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sudo sh
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
newgrp docker
ubuntu.note: The script adds Docker's official apt repo. Log out and back in if `docker ps` still says permission denied.

fedora.code:
sudo dnf -y install dnf-plugins-core
sudo dnf config-manager addrepo --from-repofile=https://download.docker.com/linux/fedora/docker-ce.repo
sudo dnf install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin
sudo systemctl enable --now docker
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER && newgrp docker
fedora.note: On RHEL / Rocky / Alma use `sudo dnf config-manager --add-repo https://download.docker.com/linux/rhel/docker-ce.repo` for the repo line.

arch.code:
sudo pacman -S --needed docker
sudo systemctl enable --now docker
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER && newgrp docker

tools.name: kind
tools.what: Kubernetes IN Docker. Creates single- or multi-node clusters on your laptop in about a minute.

windows.note: Alternative with Chocolatey: `choco install kind`. Open a new terminal afterwards so PATH refreshes.

ubuntu.code:
ARCH=$(uname -m | sed 's/x86_64/amd64/;s/aarch64/arm64/')
curl -Lo ./kind "https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kind/releases/latest/download/kind-linux-${ARCH}"
sudo install -m 0755 kind /usr/local/bin/kind && rm kind

fedora.code:
ARCH=$(uname -m | sed 's/x86_64/amd64/;s/aarch64/arm64/')
curl -Lo ./kind "https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kind/releases/latest/download/kind-linux-${ARCH}"
sudo install -m 0755 kind /usr/local/bin/kind && rm kind

arch.note: If your mirror lacks it, use the generic binary from the Ubuntu tab or `go install sigs.k8s.io/kind@latest`.

tools.name: kubectl
tools.what: The Kubernetes command-line client. Every lab talks to the cluster through it.

ubuntu.code:
ARCH=$(uname -m | sed 's/x86_64/amd64/;s/aarch64/arm64/')
curl -LO "https://dl.k8s.io/release/$(curl -Ls https://dl.k8s.io/release/stable.txt)/bin/linux/${ARCH}/kubectl"
sudo install -o root -g root -m 0755 kubectl /usr/local/bin/kubectl && rm kubectl

fedora.code:
ARCH=$(uname -m | sed 's/x86_64/amd64/;s/aarch64/arm64/')
curl -LO "https://dl.k8s.io/release/$(curl -Ls https://dl.k8s.io/release/stable.txt)/bin/linux/${ARCH}/kubectl"
sudo install -o root -g root -m 0755 kubectl /usr/local/bin/kubectl && rm kubectl

tools.name: Go
tools.what: Needed to build controllers with client-go and operators with kubebuilder.

ubuntu.code:
ARCH=$(uname -m | sed 's/x86_64/amd64/;s/aarch64/arm64/')
GO_VER=$(curl -s 'https://go.dev/VERSION?m=text' | head -n1)
curl -LO "https://go.dev/dl/${GO_VER}.linux-${ARCH}.tar.gz"
sudo rm -rf /usr/local/go && sudo tar -C /usr/local -xzf "${GO_VER}.linux-${ARCH}.tar.gz"
echo 'export PATH=$PATH:/usr/local/go/bin:$HOME/go/bin' >> ~/.bashrc && source ~/.bashrc
ubuntu.note: The apt `golang` package is often several versions behind; client-go needs a recent Go.

fedora.code:
sudo dnf install -y golang
echo 'export PATH=$PATH:$HOME/go/bin' >> ~/.bashrc && source ~/.bashrc

arch.code:
sudo pacman -S --needed go
echo 'export PATH=$PATH:$HOME/go/bin' >> ~/.bashrc && source ~/.bashrc

tools.name: kubebuilder + make
tools.what: Scaffolds operators and generates CRD YAML from Go types. Needs Go and make.

mac.code:
xcode-select --install   # provides make
brew install kubebuilder

windows.note: kubebuilder has no native Windows build. Open the Ubuntu (WSL2) terminal and follow the Ubuntu / Debian tab for Go, kubectl and kubebuilder. Docker Desktop's WSL integration lets WSL use the same Docker.

ubuntu.code:
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y make build-essential
curl -L -o kubebuilder "https://go.kubebuilder.io/dl/latest/$(go env GOOS)/$(go env GOARCH)"
sudo install -m 0755 kubebuilder /usr/local/bin/kubebuilder && rm kubebuilder

fedora.code:
sudo dnf install -y make gcc
curl -L -o kubebuilder "https://go.kubebuilder.io/dl/latest/$(go env GOOS)/$(go env GOARCH)"
sudo install -m 0755 kubebuilder /usr/local/bin/kubebuilder && rm kubebuilder

arch.code:
sudo pacman -S --needed base-devel
curl -L -o kubebuilder "https://go.kubebuilder.io/dl/latest/$(go env GOOS)/$(go env GOARCH)"
sudo install -m 0755 kubebuilder /usr/local/bin/kubebuilder && rm kubebuilder

tools.name: Node.js LTS + Yarn
tools.what: Backstage, the developer portal, is a Node.js app. Use an LTS release and enable Yarn through corepack.

ubuntu.code:

source ~/.bashrc
nvm install --lts
corepack enable
